guideText: Create states with +. Use the arrow to connect source and target. Empty transitions mean ε. FA accepts after consuming all input in a final state. PDA: top at left, initially empty stack, final-state acceptance. Turing: blank □; L left, R right, S stay; final-state acceptance. Limits: 500 steps and 2,000 configurations per level. Grammars use Earley recognition. JFLAP import: finite, pushdown and single-tape Turing automata. L-systems, circuits, cellular automata, multi-tape Turing and full JFLAP parity are not included.
lessonFA: A finite automaton stores a finite amount of information. Double circles indicate acceptance; an external arrow marks the start. A DFA has at most one choice per symbol; an NFA may have several, including ε.
lessonPDA: The stack adds memory. Its top is at the left: reading a, popping A and pushing BB replaces top A with BB. The example uses Z as a bottom marker.
lessonTM: The tape provides read/write memory. Each transition reads a symbol, writes one and moves the head. The example swaps 0 and 1 until it reaches □.
intro: Build models, explore transitions and follow every step.
